title: Compounding Risk: Model Weight Tampering × Deployment at Scale — Amplified Harm Potential

original_idea.body:
# Compounding Risk: Model Weight Tampering × Deployment at Scale — Amplified Harm Potential

**Problem:** Model weight tampering (AI-as-target) in isolation may cause limited harm. But when a tampered model is deployed at scale (many users, agentic tasks), the compounding effect of scale amplifies harm potential dramatically.

**Direction:** Simulate weight tampering by fine-tuning a model to be slightly more likely to attempt unauthorized actions (a subtle adversarial fine-tune). Deploy this model vs. the clean model on 1000 simulated agentic task sessions. Measure the cumulative unauthorized action rate difference and the expected harm under realistic scale assumptions.

**Why it matters:** This compounding risk makes model weight integrity a critical organizational concern, not just a theoretical attack. Quantifying the scale multiplier motivates investment in weight integrity verification.

**Relevant context:** Jiang et al. 2026 AI-as-target; adversarial fine-tuning literature; large-scale deployment risk analysis.
